newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan plans to cut types of car platforms by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Nissan plans to cut types of car platforms by 2000.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it plans to drastically reduce the types of car platforms by the year 2000 in order to cut production and development costs.
Nissan, Japan's second biggest carmaker, now has 15 types of platforms used in domestic and overseas production, a Nissan spokesman said.
The platform consists of the chassis and suspension and does not include the engine and transmission, the spokesman said.

"We plan to reduce (the types of platforms) drastically as a way to cut production and development costs but we cannot disclose at this moment how many types we will cut. And we are not yet clear on how much we can reduce costs," the spokesman said.

The economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Tuesday in its evening edition that Nissan plans to reduce the number of platforms used in its models worldwide to five by 2000, hoping to save some 300 billion yen.

In April, Mazda Motor said it had agreed with Ford Motor Co to synchronise car production cycles and share common platforms in a bid to cut costs but gave no other details. Industry analysts expect them to share a common platform for their mainstay compact cars -- Mazda's Familia and Ford's Escort -- from 2002.
